overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the Board's practice of deleting audio recordings after minutes are approved is governed by records retention law, and the July 17 minutes accurately summarized the chair's report on counsel's letter.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board's practice of destroying audio recordings of meetings once minutes are approved violates the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that public bodies record their meetings, nor does it address retention of audio recordings of meetings.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the July 17 minutes were insufficiently detailed because they did not explain why town counsel approved the Board's audio recording practice.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the minutes satisfy the requirements of the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
